types.name: VolumeComponent
types.doc:
Zone-based post-process override (HDRP Volume analogue).

A `VolumeComponent` contributes its profile to the per-camera blend each
frame. Two shapes:
- Global (isGlobal = true): always contributes, just sorted by priority.
- Local  (isGlobal = false): uses the entity's TransformComponent
world position + `halfExtents` as a box
AABB; contributes when the camera is
inside, with a `blendDistance` falloff at
the box edges for a soft transition.

The profile itself can live either inline on the component (`profile`,
the field directly below) or as a `.volume` asset referenced by
`profileAssetPath` (resolved by VolumeManager — when both are present,
asset wins). The inline profile is the default so new components light
up without an asset round-trip.

members.name: halfExtents
members.doc:
Box half-extents in local space. Only consulted when isGlobal=false.
World transform comes from the entity's TransformComponent — the box
ride along with the entity's position + rotation.

members.name: priority
members.doc:
Volumes are processed from low to high priority. Higher-priority
volumes override lower-priority slots that aren't already covered by
a stronger contribution. For two volumes at equal priority, the
later-walked one wins (registration order).

members.name: blendDistance
members.doc:
Distance (in world units) outside the box AABB where the volume's
influence fades from 1 to 0. Inside the box minus blendDistance
weight is 1; from there to the box edge it falls off linearly.
Ignored when isGlobal=true (global volumes always contribute at
weight*1.0).

members.name: weight
members.doc:
Per-volume strength multiplier on the camera-space weight (0..1).
Useful for scripts cross-fading two cinematic volumes — set weight
at runtime to scrub between them without changing priority order.

members.name: profileAssetPath
members.doc:
Optional asset reference — when non-empty, VolumeManager loads the
referenced VolumeProfileAsset and uses its profile instead of the
inline one below.

members.name: profile
members.doc:
Inline profile — edited via the custom HDRP-style override-toggle
UI, not via the codegen-generated property panel. We tag it as
a custom property type and keep it hidden so the codegen emits a
`PropertyType::Custom` entry with key "VolumeProfile" and skips
trying to introspect the struct's fields. Serialization is handled
by a custom struct hook; the inspector hook reads/writes this
field directly.

free.doc:

types.name: VolumeManager
types.doc:
Per-frame volume evaluator.

VolumeManager owns no state of its own — it walks the world's
VolumeComponent entities each call and computes a blended VolumeProfile
using the camera's world position. The result is materialized into a
ScenePostProcess (the renderer's existing input contract) so the existing
rendering path picks up the blended values with no further changes.

Algorithm (per Evaluate call):
1. Seed the result profile from the scene's baseline ScenePostProcess
(all slots marked overriding → backwards compat when no volumes exist).
2. Collect every enabled VolumeComponent + its TransformComponent.
3. Compute per-volume weight in [0,1]:
- global → weight = component.weight
- local  → distanceToBox / blendDistance fade, multiplied by weight
4. Sort by ascending priority (lower first), so higher-priority volumes
overwrite earlier slot values.
5. For each (volume, weight) pair, walk the profile's slots and merge:
- bool/int/enum: snap to source when overrides && weight ≥ 0.5
- float / Vec3 : lerp current → source by weight
6. Materialize the blended profile into `out`.

Designed to run unconditionally each frame — when no volumes exist the
cost is one ScenePostProcess copy and the world's component iterator
returning empty, both negligible.

members.name: Evaluate
members.signature: static void Evaluate(World& world, const Vec3& cameraPos, const ScenePostProcess& seedDefaults, ScenePostProcess& outPostProcess)
members.doc:
Walk the world, compute the blended profile at `cameraPos`, and write
the result into `outPostProcess`. `seedDefaults` is the scene's
baseline (Scene::Environment().postProcess) used as the seed so the
path is backwards-compatible.

members.name: EvaluateProfile
members.signature: static VolumeProfile EvaluateProfile(World& world, const Vec3& cameraPos, const VolumeProfile& seed)
members.doc:
Lower-level — produces the blended VolumeProfile without writing back
to a ScenePostProcess. Useful for tooling and tests.

members.name: Blend
members.signature: static void Blend(VolumeProfile& dst, const VolumeProfile& src, float weight)
members.doc:
Merge one profile's overriding slots into another at `weight`, with the
per-type rules above. Public because the Volume Profile editor shows
what a given blend weight resolves to, and a preview computed by a
second copy of these rules is a preview of something the renderer never
produces.

members.name: SetPreviewProfile
members.doc:
Editor preview. While a profile is set it blends LAST at full weight,
above every authored volume, so an open .volume document is what the
viewport shows without the author first having to place a volume around
the camera. Only the editor sets this.

types.name: VolumeOverride
types.doc:
HDRP-style per-parameter override slot. `value` is read by the renderer
only when `overrides` is true; otherwise the underlying scene default or
the last volume to override wins.

We deliberately do NOT default-initialize `value` — VolumeProfile sets
each slot's value explicitly so the defaults match ScenePostProcess.

members.name: VolumeOverride
members.signature: explicit VolumeOverride(const T& v) : overrides(false), value(v)

members.name: VolumeOverride
members.signature: VolumeOverride(bool ov, const T& v) : overrides(ov), value(v)

types.name: VolumeProfile
types.doc:
Mirror of ScenePostProcess where every parameter is wrapped in
VolumeOverride<T>. A profile authored by the user only flips `overrides`
on the fields they care about — everything else falls through to the
scene's baseline ScenePostProcess. VolumeManager produces a blended
VolumeProfile per frame; SceneRenderer then materializes the result into
ScenePostProcess for the existing render path to read.

Field order mirrors ScenePostProcess (Scene.h) — keep them in sync if you
add a field there. Add the corresponding VolumeOverride here AND the lerp
in VolumeManager::BlendInto.

members.name: MakeProfileFromScenePostProcess
members.doc:
Copies the scene's baseline ScenePostProcess into a profile where every
slot is marked as overriding (so a downstream blend starting from this
profile sees full coverage). Used by VolumeManager to seed the result
before walking volumes, so without any volumes the renderer sees today's
ScenePostProcess unchanged.

members.name: ApplyProfileToScenePostProcess
members.signature: static void ApplyProfileToScenePostProcess(const VolumeProfile& profile, ScenePostProcess& out)
members.doc:
Inverse — materializes a (blended) VolumeProfile back into a
ScenePostProcess for the existing render path. Fields that aren't
overridden in the profile are left as-is in `out`.

members.name: autoExposureMetering
members.doc:
Auto exposure. The floor/ceiling pair belongs on a volume above all the
others here: a horror level wants the ceiling brought right down inside
the dark rooms and released again outdoors, and that is a per-room
decision, not a per-scene one. Metering mode is discrete (it selects a
statistic, and there is nothing between two statistics to blend).

types.name: FVolumeProfileSerialize
types.doc:
Single source of truth for VolumeProfile MDF I/O. Used both by
VolumeProfileAsset (loading a .volume from disk) and the VolumeComponent
custom-serialize hook (storing inline profiles inside scene MDFs).

On the wire each overridden slot is a sub-node of the form
<slotName overrides="true" value="X"/>
Slots that aren't overriding are simply omitted, keeping authored files
small — a "do nothing" profile is empty MDF.
